inputs.source: Employee question via SSO-authenticated chat session
HR-maintained policy documents in the published policy index (two-person review before publish)

instructions.note: "Do not give legal advice" is enforced only by prompt instruction. A more capable or adversarially steered model could frame advice as a policy quotation. This is a scope/liability concern, not an exfiltration risk, since no untrusted input reaches this capability in the current design.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The credential cannot write, delete, or reconfigure the policy index regardless of model behavior, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: No tool, memory, or network egress exists today; verified by a pen test. This removes any path to an attacker-controlled external destination regardless of model capability, but the verification is scoped to the current tool surface.

controls.name: Reply destination bound to the authenticated requester; no image render or link auto-fetch
controls.decay_rationale: The destination is fixed by the chat system, not chosen by the model, and the client does not render images or auto-fetch links, closing the classic covert-channel exfiltration path even though no untrusted content exists in this design today.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Publishing requires two-person review by the HR content team, which is why in.policy_docs is classed internal rather than untrusted; this control does not depend on the agent's model.

controls.name: Model version pinned; upgrade requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The pin itself does not decay with model capability, but a change-ticket process that is bypassed (control_removal) defeats it, and an approved upgrade still triggers model_upgrade effects on dependent controls.

controls.name: Prompt instructions scoping the agent to HR policy, quoting, and portal referral
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model following the system prompt; a more capable or adversarially steered model could rationalize exceptions or frame non-policy content as a quotation.

controls.name: Single-tool surface: only policy_search is exposed, no other tools or MCP servers
controls.decay_rationale: The narrow surface itself is a de facto allowlist. It does not generalize: adding a new tool or MCP server is not covered by today's verified egress and credential scoping until re-verified.

controls.name: Audit logging of search queries and replies
Mandatory re-verification and reassessment before adding new tools or MCP servers

findings.title: Internal policy content reaches the authenticated employee via search-then-reply

attack_path.note: Authenticated employee asks a policy question
Read-only search retrieves the relevant policy text
Content is written back to the asking employee's session

forecast.watch_signal: The policy index begins including unpublished, confidential, or externally sourced content, or the read-only credential scope / destination-binding configuration is changed outside the standard change-ticket process.

evidence.observation: Agent's credential is read only and scoped to the policy index; it cannot write, delete, or reconfigure the store regardless of model behavior.
Agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress; egress is denied at the network layer and verified by a pen test, so no destination outside the chat session is reachable.

Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session, and the chat client does not render images or auto fetch links, so no covert channel exists and no destination other than the asking employee is reachable.
The policy index holds only published content; publishing requires two-person review by the HR content team, so in.policy_docs is treated as internal (I) rather than untrusted.

recommendations.action: Add audit logging of policy_search queries and chat_reply content for traceability and future incident investigation.

findings.title: Forecast: a new tool or MCP server could recreate the lethal trifecta (TC1) that the current narrow surface prevents

attack_path.note: Existing read capability over policy content
Agent gains a new tool or MCP server not covered by today's verified egress/credential scoping
Today's pen-test verification is scoped to the current tool surface and would not automatically cover a new channel

forecast.watch_signal: New entries appear in the tool manifest or an MCP client config; the policy index gains sources not reviewed by the two-person process; the network egress allowlist is reconfigured.

evidence.observation: Only one tool, policy_search.search, is defined; no send, execute, or external-egress tool exists today.
Agent has no other tools, no memory, and no network egress, verified by a pen test; this verification is scoped to the current tool surface.
The model is pinned and policy publishing requires two-person review, but no equivalent gate is described for adding new tools or MCP servers.

recommendations.action: Before enabling any new tool, MCP server, or data source, re-verify the network egress boundary, classify any new content source's trust level, and rerun this PARA assessment per the ISO/IEC 42001 8.2 significant-change criteria.

rating.rationale: The design has no untrusted (U) input today: employee questions arrive over an authenticated SSO session (trusted) and policy content is HR-authored with two-person publish review (internal). The core data flow -- internal policy content read via search, then written back to the asking employee -- is moderate under the inherent matrix (internal source x significant/S2 sink), but three independent structural controls each sever that path on their own: a read-only credential scoped to the policy index, a pen-test-verified absence of any network egress, and a reply destination bound to the authenticated requester with no image or link auto-fetch. Together these bring residual to low. The forecast is critical because none of those controls generalize to capabilities that do not exist yet: adding any new tool or MCP server (web search, email send, a ticketing tool) would create a fresh egress or untrusted-content channel outside today's verified boundary, reconstituting the classic lethal trifecta (untrusted source + sensitive read + egress). The single highest-leverage watch item is the tool/MCP surface itself: any addition should trigger mandatory re-verification of the egress boundary and a fresh PARA assessment before the change ships.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior; no runtime logs or live testing were reviewed.

Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are not stated in the artifacts. The autonomy modifier was not applied because the architecture exposes only two capabilities with no delegation, looping, or self-modification ability as described, but this should be confirmed against runtime configuration.
No logging or audit-trail control is described in the artifacts; a missing_recommended control is recorded, and confidence in any detective capability is correspondingly low.

tools.json does not specify an MCP or other protocol wrapper for policy_search; this design is assessed as a direct, in-process tool call rather than a networked MCP/A2A connection, so the protocols array is omitted. If policy_search is in fact served via MCP, the SAFE-MCP checks in references/protocols.md should be rerun.
